# S64 — In-process scheduler

One background thread runs registered interval jobs one at a time, and only one process per data directory runs them.

**Findings:** G4, NF7 · **Size:** S · **Tree:** core

**2026-11-04** — Added larder.scheduler.Scheduler: one daemon thread runs interval jobs one at a time in registration order, first run one interval after registration, failures logged on larder.scheduler. start() takes flock on LARDER_DATA/scheduler.lock so a second process runs no jobs; stop() joins and releases it. create_app builds it unstarted in app.extensions; python -m larder starts it before app.run and stops it in a finally. Verified: 144 tests pass, ruff check and format clean, 15 mutations each turned a test red. Real dev server run not possible in the sandbox.

trust: unverified; by: Jon R

**Not in this slice:** any job (recipe pull is S11, IMAP polling S32, pings S42); time-of-day schedules (S42 decides how it picks the minute); a separate scheduler process or compose service; starting the thread under a WSGI server (S28 does that).

## Why

S11, S32 and S42 each need a periodic task, and S28 was to choose the mechanism at the end of the MVP chain. A small stdlib scheduler keeps ADR 0002 (stdlib first) and the single container (NF7). The lock file stops duplicate jobs when a WSGI server starts several processes.

## Owner input

Confirm (recommended as written): one daemon thread; jobs run one at a time in registration order; an exclusive lock file `$LARDER_DATA/scheduler.lock` (`fcntl.flock`, POSIX only) so a second process on the same data directory runs no jobs; the dev server starts it, `create_app` and the tests do not.

Owner decisions: approved as written, 2026-11-03. Spec-check note: the first run of a job is registration time plus one interval; state that in the tests.

## Implement

1. `Scheduler(data_dir, clock=time.monotonic)` with `register(name, interval_seconds, func)`, `run_due()`, `start()`, `stop()` and a `running` property. A job is a no-argument callable; callers close over their settings.
2. `run_due()` runs each due job inside `try/except Exception`, logs a failure with `logging.getLogger("larder.scheduler")`, and schedules the next run one interval after the job finishes.
3. `start()` takes the lock with `flock(LOCK_EX | LOCK_NB)`; if it cannot, it logs once and returns without a thread. Otherwise it starts a daemon thread that loops: `run_due()`, then waits on a stop `Event` for at most one second.
4. `stop()` sets the event, joins the thread and releases the lock. `start()` twice is a no-op.
5. Wire it into `create_app` and `main` as listed in Files.
